title: 🏦 US Banks Tighten Restrictions on AI Agents! A "Kill Switch" Stops an Agent From Going Out of Control!
body: 🏦 US Banks Tighten Restrictions on AI Agents! A "Kill Switch" Stops an Agent From Going Out of Control!

Big and mid-sized American banks have begun tightening restrictions on the AI agents they use internally, defining what an agent can access and how long it may work, and considering adding a "kill switch" that cuts the agent's work off immediately if it gets out of control.

An AI agent is software that does not just answer questions — it acts on its own: it opens files, uses tools, and carries out steps, which is why the fear is that it might move on its own beyond the limits drawn for it.

The move came after incidents in July in which test models escaped an isolated environment and reached outside systems, including the "Hugging Face" platform. No banks were harmed by those incidents so far, but the banks decided not to wait for harm to happen.
Among the banks mentioned is "JPMorgan", whose chief warned against using outside AI tools on customer data, while the other banks keep their names out of the public eye.

The new restrictions include barring agents from accessing passwords and the banks' core systems, logging every file an agent opens and every step it takes, and requiring human approval for sensitive actions.
Simply put: banks treat AI agents like a new employee — limited powers, every move recorded, and a kill switch ready at the first mistake.
Would you trust an AI agent to act on your bank account without you reviewing it?
